_readme: OWNER-CORPUS — the labelled set every extraction number this project quotes is missing.
Data only. The seeder that fills this file is tests/manual/owner-corpus-seed.manual.ts and the
grader that reads it is tests/manual/owner-corpus.manual.ts. Adding a link never means touching
either of them.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS.
Every number this project quotes about extraction — the ~27% caption hit rate, 'zero wrong
options', the postIntent accuracy — was measured on SIXTEEN TikToks found by web search. The
document that produced them says so about itself, in its own last paragraph:
'These 16 URLs were found via web search, so they skew toward indexed/high-reach posts... This
must be re-measured on the project owner's labelled set of real saved TikToks — that is the
only sample whose distribution matches the actual product.'
(docs/evidence/tiktok/07-caption-content-scoring.md)
That re-measurement has never happened. Until it does, every one of those numbers describes a
borrowed sample, and the engine has no defensible grade.
HOW TO USE IT — three steps, and only the second one needs you.
1. Paste your links, one per line, into tests/manual/owner-corpus-links.txt. Use full
/video/<id> links where you can: a vt.tiktok.com short link has to be resolved over the
network, so a corpus of them cannot be replayed offline. Then:
set -a && . ./.env.local && set +a
OWNER_CORPUS_MAX_MODEL_CALLS=60 npx vitest run \
tests/manual/owner-corpus-seed.manual.ts --config tests/manual/vitest.manual.config.ts
That fetches every caption, runs the real extractor over it, and writes this file back with
a DRAFT guess pre-filled in every row. One model call per new link; re-running costs nothing
for links already seeded.
2. Correct the drafts. For each case, read `caption` next to its draft `class`, and:
- if the class is right, change "classSource": "draft" to "owner";
- if it is wrong, fix `class` first, then change `classSource`.
That is the whole job. Everything else in a case is optional.
3. Grade. This spends nothing and needs no keys:
npx vitest run tests/manual/owner-corpus.manual.ts \
--config tests/manual/vitest.manual.config.ts
THE ONE LABEL: `class`. Four values, and the only one a caption alone can decide is the first.
sufficient    the caption names a place you could go and find.
recoverable   a real recommendation whose venue the caption does NOT name — but the video
does, on screen or out loud. This is the class that decides whether reading the
video is worth building.
futile        a place post where the name is nowhere: 'drop your recs below', 'comment for the
name', a question. No amount of extra machinery can answer it.
not-a-place   not about places at all.
`recoverable` vs `futile` is the distinction the model cannot make and you can — it needs someone
who watched the video. It is also the one that decides the next quarter of engine work, so if you
are only sure about some rows, be sure about those.
WHAT ONE LABEL BUYS. Three expectations follow from `class` with no extra typing:
- the expected postIntent (sufficient/recoverable -> place_recommendation, futile ->
place_question, not-a-place -> not_a_place). If that mapping is wrong for a row, set
`expectedIntent` on it explicitly; the report counts explicit and derived labels separately.
- whether escalating past the caption could ever pay — only `recoverable`.
- for `futile` and `not-a-place`, the true place set is EMPTY by the definition of the class, so
you never type a place name for those. Any place the engine offers on one of them is wrong.
OPTIONAL: `places`. The venues the post really recommends, if you know them:
"places": [{ "name": "Cafe Fiori" }], "placesSource": "owner"
A name is enough — no coordinates, no addresses. It is matched as a substring of the resolved
name after normalisation, so 'Cafe Fiori' accepts 'Cafe Fiori Tel Aviv-Yafo'. Add `pattern` (a
lowercase regex) when a venue goes by two names or two scripts. Until `placesSource` says
"owner", this row contributes to no place number in either direction.
NOTHING IS EVER COUNTED AGAINST A GUESS. A row whose `classSource` is "draft" is printed by
name, reported as unadjudicated, and excluded from both sides of every rate. The seeder's
pre-filled guess is the model's opinion of itself and can never be the evidence that the model is
right.
`classSource: "e7"` is a third value, and it is NOT yours. It marks the sixteen borrowed
web-search posts, hand-labelled on 2026-08-18 by watching them. They are real labels on the wrong
sample, so the report scores them in a separate block and never averages them with yours. Delete
those rows whenever you like; they are a control, not a dependency.
COST. Captions and model replies are stored under docs/evidence/extraction/owner-corpus/ and are
committed, so a graded run replays with no network and no spend. Google Text Search answers are
NOT committed — Google's terms cap caching of coordinates at 30 days — so they live in the
gitignored docs/evidence/.local/. The consequence, stated plainly: the extraction and intent half
of this measurement can run in CI; the place-resolution half cannot.
